prize_parts.citation: For the development of ligand-controlled palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, making the synthesis of aryl amines general and routine.

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the clearest case on the list of a general method that changed how chemists build bonds. Bulky biaryl and hindered alkyl phosphine ligands turned aryl amination from a narrow, harsh reaction into a routine operation across amine and aryl-halide classes. Its adoption is visible in the literature, in countless total and medicinal syntheses, and in pharmaceutical process routes. It is thirty years mature, with several ligand and precatalyst generations independently confirmed. Buchwald and Hartwig developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled method and its mechanistic basis independently, so a two-person prize is clean.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize already honoured Pd cross-coupling, so some members will see C-N coupling as an extension of a prize already given and not a new principle. Kosugi's tin-amide work precedes the catalytic method, which leaves a priority question that a two-person prize does not resolve. Support for B021 in the openings is also narrow (two first places, then ranks 5 and 7), and it sits well below the biology-facing candidates in Borda points.

responses.point: Zou ranks B021 first as an enabling method adopted by a whole community, with Kosugi's tin-amide chemistry as a precursor and a priority question, not an equal claim.
responses.response: I agree on both points. The precursor needed stoichiometric tin amides and had narrow scope. The catalytic, ligand-controlled general method is what changed practice, and that is what the citation should name. I would put Kosugi in the background of the citation text, not on the laureate list. Zou's second and third choices (nanotubes, zeolites) did not reach the shortlist, so on this shortlist our views converge on B021 and little else.

responses.point: Brzezinski accepts that C-N coupling is beyond doubt important but ranks it seventh because the 2010 prize on Pd cross-coupling may reduce urgency and the mechanism is organometallic, outside his area.
responses.response: I disagree that the 2010 prize reduces the claim. That prize covered C-C coupling of organometallic nucleophiles (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki). C-N coupling has a different mechanism, with amide binding and C-N reductive elimination, and needed its own ligand design. It also opened a different bond class, so a pure-chemistry committee should not treat it as a repeat. I do accept his point that this is organometallic mechanism and not biochemistry, and I would not claim it as a physical-organic advance. I also do not share his top choice, B017: long-range protein electron transfer is rigorous, but it does not rank above the general-method impact of B021.

responses.point: Sparr ranks B021 fifth as a clear, general, practical methodology, but notes the 2010 prize honoured Pd cross-coupling broadly. She ranks phase separation (B044) and lipid nanoparticles (B058) first and second.
responses.response: On the 2010 precedent I make the same argument as above: the bond formed is new, and the ligand design is the advance. On B044 I ask the question I ask of border-field nominations, namely what was new chemically. Phase separation is a conceptual reframing in cell biology with strong physical chemistry. The chemical advance is less sharply identifiable than a general catalyst. I take her B058 case more seriously, because pKa-tuned ionizable lipids are a molecular design principle. My doubt there is attribution: six credited names and a three-person cap.

responses.point: Aili ranks sequencing-by-synthesis (B028) first because the reversible-terminator chemistry and surface chemistry changed genomics and clinical practice, with Balasubramanian and Klenerman as the core.
responses.response: The impact is not in doubt. My reservation is the chemistry-versus-technology line. The nucleotide chemistry is real, but the prize-relevant achievement is a platform in which optics, engineering and commercial competition all matter, and the credit among Solexa, 454, Ju and Mayer is contested. A prize that cleanly credits one chemical advance seems safer to me. If the committee goes towards biology-facing chemistry, I would favour B052, where the deaminase chemistry has one clearly identifiable intellectual driver.

uncertainties: Whether the committee treats the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize as a bar to C-N coupling. I think the novelty is clear but several colleagues weigh it more heavily.
Whether Kosugi should be credited in the citation or among the laureates; I rely on memory for the precise chronology and have not verified it.
Whether a two-achievement prize pairing B021 with a biology-facing candidate (B052 or B058) would command more votes than B021 alone.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B021. I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or Kosugi. My general professional proximity to synthetic methodology is not a recusal issue.
